public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
General Intuition operates in the AI & Software sector at an undisclosed stage. The relevant comp universe consists of one public peer (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and eight private companies, including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. This universe spans multiple development and commercialization phases within frontier AI.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The analysis identified 12 same-sector peers but found zero matches meeting narrow stage-alignment or valuation-tier criteria. Filtering for same-stage comparables, adjacent-stage comparables, or similar-tier private companies each yielded fewer than three datapoints—below the minimum threshold of three observations required for reliable median estimation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias given the heterogeneity in business model, capital intensity, and commercialization timeline across the broader AI & Software peer set.

With the primary triangulation method inapplicable, no single valuation range can be derived from the available data. The analysis cannot proceed to synthesis without either: additional stage clarification enabling tighter peer stratification, disclosed financial metrics (revenue, burn, headcount) permitting revenue or cost-multiple approaches, or expansion of the comparable set through adjacent-stage or related-sector peers. Key uncertainties remain the target's specific stage, revenue traction, and capital efficiency relative to the identified private comparables.
